title: Deep double descent
description: Test error can peak near interpolation before falling as capacity increases.

claims.heading: As networks grow, test error can fall, peak near exact training fits, then fall.
Test error can fall, rise, and fall again during training
More training samples can raise test error near the interpolation threshold
Risk can fall again beyond interpolation across model classes
Can one effective complexity measure predict peaks across size, epochs and samples?
Do noise and variance explain multiple peaks removed by optimally tuned overfitting controls?
Measuring effective parameters can turn double descent into a U-shaped curve

related_findings.title: Architecture changes the benefits of capacity
related_findings.summary: The benefit of added capacity depends on architecture, initialization, data structure and the solutions training selects. Parameter count alone does not order test risk.

examples.headline: At width 500, depth lowers 2-local test error but raises 2-global test error.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpolation thresholds depend on loss and effective rank
related_findings.summary: Risk peaks can follow separability, effective feature rank or local interpolation constraints. Nominal parameter and sample totals can miss these thresholds.

examples.headline: Across sample sizes, peaks track the number of independent learned-feature directions rather than nominal width.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: When interpolation helps or harms
related_findings.summary: Fitting training data exactly can yield vanishing excess error (benign), bounded positive excess error (tempered), or harmful generalization, depending on dimension, covariance spectrum, signal alignment and noise. The estimator’s assumptions also matter.

examples.headline: SGD’s bounded, positive excess error tends to vanish as input dimension grows relative to sample size.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Variance can rise and fall around interpolation
related_findings.summary: Prediction variance and variability across training runs can peak near interpolation and decline with width. The pattern depends on how variance is decomposed and evaluated.

examples.headline: Standard and parallel ResNet-18 loss variance rises then falls, with descent beginning at width 8.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Poor conditioning can amplify interpolation risk
related_findings.summary: Nearly singular design, kernel or covariance matrices can amplify risk near interpolation. Conditioning alone does not establish a risk peak or vanishing excess error.

examples.headline: Random Fourier feature regression’s matrix becomes noninvertible at interpolation, then better conditioned as width grows.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Complexity measures track some curves
related_findings.summary: Measures derived from training can track particular double-descent curves. Their associations vary across architectures, noise levels and metrics, leaving a universal peak predictor unestablished.

examples.headline: Pruning tolerance tracks CNN and ResNet18 test loss better than the curvature-based effective parameter count.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Extra features can induce implicit regularization
related_findings.summary: Weak or noisy features, finite feature sampling and overparameterization can induce effective shrinkage. These effects resemble ridge regularization under the models' stated assumptions.

examples.headline: Low training-shot budgets suppress the interpolation peak and act as effective ridge regularization.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training duration changes the benefit of capacity
related_findings.summary: Capacity and sample size affect convergence and the best stopping time. Reaching zero label error or a late second descent need not yield the lowest test risk.

examples.headline: Longer averaged-SGD training improves synthetic random-feature generalization but remains slightly worse than minimum-norm regression.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Risk can peak as regularization changes
related_findings.summary: Risk can be non-monotone as explicit regularization or optimizer temperature changes. The best penalty depends on noise, spectrum, class balance and the evaluation objective.

examples.headline: A spherical normalizing flow’s reverse Kullback–Leibler divergence peaks; its maximum a posteriori curve lacks second descent.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Ensemble design changes interpolation peaks
related_findings.summary: Averaging, subsampling and ensemble weights can suppress peaks or change risk. An optimized ensemble under a fixed budget need not outperform a single model.

examples.headline: Score averaging beats majority vote for three random-feature logistic models; infinite ensembles erase the difference.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpolation guarantees depend on specific assumptions
related_findings.summary: Generalization guarantees for interpolators depend on spectral, geometric and algorithmic assumptions. Specialized bounds can describe settings that conventional capacity arguments miss.

examples.headline: An architecture-independent bound applies to explicitly constructed zero-loss ReLU minimizers under stated assumptions.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sensitivity and boundary fragmentation can peak
related_findings.summary: Input sensitivity and decision-region fragmentation can peak near interpolation and decline afterward. Regularization or changes in data geometry can separate these patterns from test risk.

examples.headline: Lower bounds on input sensitivity rise during training, whereas sensitivity peaks when model width varies.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Clean generalization does not ensure adversarial robustness
related_findings.summary: Interpolation and continued training can worsen adversarial risk even when excess error on clean data vanishes. Attack norm, perturbation size, activation and stopping rule affect the outcome.

examples.headline: At radius 0.1 in Case 2, additional samples worsen SI loss but improve LP risk.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature order can generate multiple descents
related_findings.summary: Feature inclusion order, target alignment and spectral learning stages can generate non-monotone or staircase risk curves. These patterns need not involve a single interpolation transition.

examples.headline: With zero noise, misordered feature inclusion produces multiple descents entirely below interpolation.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Pruning changes risk beyond parameter reduction
related_findings.summary: Pruning and sparsity sweeps can produce additional risk minima and peaks. Their locations and benefits depend on initialization, training, label noise and distillation.

examples.headline: Generative-audio masking and trimming errors reach minima after substantial parameter removal.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Late overfitting need not recover
related_findings.summary: Some noisy-label or excess-capacity models show late degradation without recovery within the reported training horizon. Noise, data structure and regularization affect this behavior.

examples.headline: Final error rises with label corruption; minimum error stays flat before rising at higher corruption.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Unequal learning speeds can generate temporal peaks
related_findings.summary: Features learned at different speeds can produce epoch-wise peaks. Aligning their learning rates or regularization can remove peaks and improve the best early-stopped performance.

examples.headline: Rescaling layer step sizes eliminates CNN epoch-wise double descent and improves best early-stopped performance.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Delayed generalization need not reflect interpolation
related_findings.summary: Delayed generalization and sharp learning transitions depend on data amount, model size, initialization and separability. Their appearance does not establish interpolation-driven double descent.

examples.headline: With large initialization and small weight decay, IMDB accuracy improves long after training-set fitting.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Additional data can hurt away from interpolation
related_findings.summary: Misspecification, robust objectives or contamination can make additional samples increase risk away from interpolation thresholds. The effect depends on the learner.

examples.headline: Optimally tuned ridge has higher expected risk with two samples than one under heteroscedasticity.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Representation geometry changes around generalization transitions
related_findings.summary: Representation rank, compression and alignment across networks can change around generalization transitions. Their relationship to risk depends on noise, task and training stage.

examples.headline: Some weight-decay settings yield staged MNIST accuracy gains alongside double descent in MLP feature ranks.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Curvature and training dynamics can track risk
related_findings.summary: Some risk peaks and recoveries coincide with changes in curvature, parameter displacement, connectivity or dynamical stability. These associations have exceptions across settings.

examples.headline: The study’s loss-sharpness measure tracks noisy-label validation error across widths better than the effective parameter count.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Data repetition can produce risk peaks
related_findings.summary: Repeated or near-duplicate data can produce risk peaks and degradation associated with replay. Deduplication, data order and regularization alter the effect.

examples.headline: At fixed compute and repeated-token fraction, intermediate repetition raises evaluation loss above the no-repetition baseline.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Some learning curves improve without a peak
related_findings.summary: Some learners and data regimes show monotone or saturating gains from additional samples, training time or width. No double-descent peak is reported in those settings.

examples.headline: LC-Net JPEG-steganalysis accuracy improves with more training images, with a fitted error floor.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Optimal ridge can be zero or negative
related_findings.summary: Beyond interpolation, covariance alignment and implicit shrinkage can make zero or negative ridge penalties optimal. Positive ridge does not always improve risk.

examples.headline: Negative ridge improves some MNIST fits but causes diverging risk peaks in others.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Norm peaks do not determine risk peaks
related_findings.summary: Minimum-norm predictor norms often peak near interpolation and decline afterward. A norm peak can also occur when test risk is monotone.

examples.headline: The estimator norm can peak even when risk remains monotone.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Distribution shift changes the value of data
related_findings.summary: Distribution shift changes the benefits of capacity, data and regularization. Additional training samples or longer contexts can harm performance on the target distribution.

examples.headline: For in-distribution-tuned isotropic ridge, distribution shift determines whether additional samples help or hurt.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Evaluation metrics can disagree about overfitting
related_findings.summary: Held-out loss, accuracy, generalization gap and ranking metrics can show different curves. Evaluation-label noise, loss geometry and calibration can change the visible pattern.

examples.headline: DeepSurv log-risk norms increasingly exceed the true log-hazard norm as training loss falls.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpolation and evaluation design matter
related_findings.summary: Observing a peak depends on whether the estimator actually interpolates and whether evaluation uses unseen data. Non-interpolating models or full-data evaluation can lack a peak.

examples.headline: GIN molecular-property models retain training error and show single U-shaped test-error curves across tested dimensions.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Information criteria can diverge from test risk
related_findings.summary: Regret and information criteria sometimes track interpolation risk. Marginal likelihood and information efficiency can follow different curves depending on priors, spectra and tuning.

examples.headline: Trigonometric interpolation has larger minimum-norm solution norms and regret near interpolation.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature organization changes during the second descent
related_findings.summary: Recovery under label noise involves changes in learned representations and the organization of clean and noisy features. The proposed mechanisms differ across architectures.

examples.headline: An MLP develops a large early-layer signal near second descent as clean and noisy activations separate.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training and measurement choices change observed curves
related_findings.summary: Learning rate, optimization coordinates, stochasticity and sample weighting can change generalization trajectories. Evaluation frequency can also affect which features of a curve are visible.

examples.headline: Equal training durations restore stability scaling across MNIST MLP widths.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training rebounds do not establish test-risk peaks
related_findings.summary: Optimization distance, training loss and policy entropy can follow non-monotone trajectories. These observations alone do not establish double descent in held-out risk.

examples.headline: Standard LoRA on LLaMA-2-7B shows a transient training-loss rebound that sharpens at rank 128.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generative fidelity recovery doesn’t establish interpolation with vanishing excess error
related_findings.summary: Diffusion memorization and fidelity depend on data, capacity, training time and score-matching regularization. Recovery in distributional distance does not establish that interpolating population scores yields vanishing excess error.

examples.headline: Rectified-flow CIFAR-10 FID and sliced-Wasserstein curves fall, rise, then fall identically across splits.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Average improvements can conceal subgroup harm
related_findings.summary: Aggregate scaling curves can conceal harms or benefits to particular groups. Group behavior depends on spurious correlations, covariance differences, noise allocation and the training objective.

examples.headline: Under reweighted training, larger CelebA models worsen worst-group error beyond interpolation while average error improves.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Capacity curves depend on forecasting and portfolio objectives
related_findings.summary: Portfolio Sharpe ratios and forecasting losses vary with capacity in ways that depend on objectives and signals. A second improvement need not beat a simple benchmark.

examples.headline: The studied portfolios’ Sharpe ratios fall then recover as dimension, composition and target vary.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training interventions can shift or suppress peaks
related_findings.summary: Structural constraints, group-fairness penalties and mutual-learning losses can shift or damp risk peaks. These effects occur beyond scalar ridge tuning.

examples.headline: Mutual learning (training models together) lowers the error peak across widths and shifts where overparameterization begins.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Margin bounds can fail to track test error
related_findings.summary: Overparameterization can increase sparsity or normalized margins (scale-adjusted gaps between correct and competing class scores). Yet error bounds based on those margins may still fail to track test error.

examples.headline: Margin-based test-error bounds exceed one, missing rising and falling test error in the studied settings.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Tree capacity has distinct intervention axes
related_findings.summary: Tree-ensemble curves depend on the algorithm and how capacity changes. Averaging learners and increasing the number of candidate splits can have different effects.

examples.headline: Gradient-boosted trees show double descent when candidate split counts vary, with other reported capacity settings fixed.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Exponents describing kernel convergence rates can oscillate
related_findings.summary: Kernel convergence-rate exponents and plateaus in approximation error can vary non-monotonically when sample size and dimension change together. These patterns can occur even as error decreases with sample size.

examples.headline: Spherical kernels’ optimal worst-case convergence-rate exponents alternate between peaks and valleys, distinct from error peaks.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Capacity and replay can reduce forgetting
related_findings.summary: Excess capacity can reduce catastrophic forgetting. Replay-buffer size can shift the location and severity of continual-learning scaling peaks.

examples.headline: Excess-capacity MLPs retain episodes and rules better after training on interfering associations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sparse embeddings can limit useful training
related_findings.summary: Sparse categorical embeddings can cause abrupt degradation after one epoch in click-through-rate models. Reducing feature sparsity can extend useful training.

examples.headline: Sparse-feature removal enables stable multi-epoch CTR training after validation performance reportedly peaks at epoch one.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Estimation and training losses can differ from prediction risk
related_findings.summary: Parameter-estimation error, loss when each example is held out in turn, and training-set prediction error can differ from held-out error. They need not peak, grow without bound, or reach their minimum at the same settings.

examples.headline: Normalized excess state-action loss on training data levels off at noise variance, without diverging at interpolation.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Source training can shape target risk
related_findings.summary: Interpolation in the source model (fitting all training data), along with its pretraining conditions, can shape generalization after transfer to a target model. These conditions can carry generalization patterns over to the target, delay them or reverse them.

examples.headline: The source model’s interpolation error peak also appears in targets with fewer samples than the source.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training-loss floors change overfitting trajectories
related_findings.summary: Maintaining a training-loss floor—a lower limit on training loss—can induce a second decline in ordinary held-out loss or suppress robust overfitting (worsening robustness on held-out data during training). The outcome depends on the objective and how the floor values are distributed.

examples.headline: Flooding prevents rising robust test loss in adversarial PrLM training; a 0.2 floor works best.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Held-out losses can show double descent
related_findings.summary: Model-wise second descents can appear in held-out cross-entropy or negative log-likelihood. Their visibility depends on inference and averaging methods.

examples.headline: CIFAR-100 CNN and ResNet18 width sweeps show cross-entropy test-loss double descent without stated added noise.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Calibration can diverge from prediction error
related_findings.summary: Calibration (how well confidence matches accuracy) and uncertainty in predictions given the observed data can rise and fall or plateau while prediction error improves. These calibration and uncertainty patterns can persist with regularization chosen to minimize error.

examples.headline: ScaleCNN calibration error rises then falls with width, while MobileNetV2 calibration error rises monotonically.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Task diversity and context change scaling curves
related_findings.summary: Task diversity and context length can shift or suppress generalization peaks. Longer context does not uniformly improve performance.

examples.headline: Training on games together removes or delays validation-loss peaks at intermediate model sizes.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Unstable reconstruction can destabilize model predictions over time
related_findings.summary: Reconstruction that is highly sensitive to small changes can destabilize models of reduced dimension or models that feed predictions back in to predict later states. Suitable reconstruction priors (assumptions about what is being reconstructed), noise or regularization can reduce this instability.

examples.headline: More trajectories destabilize magnetic-pendulum NGRC rollouts; suitable regularization suppresses instability, with interpolation proximity unestablished.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Downstream metrics can favor different checkpoints
related_findings.summary: Out-of-distribution detection (spotting inputs unlike the training data) and downstream-task metrics can have different optimal settings or scaling curves from test performance on data drawn from the training distribution.

examples.headline: Out-of-distribution detection peaks at intermediate training checkpoints while test accuracy on the training distribution keeps improving.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Second-descent solutions can match regularized estimators
related_findings.summary: Some solutions beyond the interpolation threshold (where training data can first be fit exactly) match transformed first-descent solutions, linear ridge regression or low-rank regularized estimators. These equivalences do not establish a full U-shaped risk curve—risk falling then rising—under a different measure of complexity.

examples.headline: The overparameterized synthetic-augmentation limit equals kernel ridge regression with a rank-k factor kernel.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Wider Bayesian models can predict worse
related_findings.summary: Increasing width in Bayesian hierarchical models can degrade prediction toward an infinite-width limit. The best width depends on mismatch between the prior and target.

examples.headline: Two-layer Bayesian NNs usually maximize UCI test log likelihood at 8–16 hidden units.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Stable accuracy can conceal individual-example forgetting
related_findings.summary: Forgetting individual held-out examples can increase with model size or reduced data even when aggregate test accuracy remains stable.

examples.headline: ResNet18 forgets a larger fraction of held-out CIFAR-100 examples with reduced training data.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Privacy changes training and stopping requirements
related_findings.summary: Privacy perturbations can introduce interpolation-related singularities in training error. They also change sample requirements and optimal stopping times.

examples.headline: With differentially private gradient descent, training wider random-feature models and MNIST networks is best stopped earlier.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Limited data can favor smaller language models
related_findings.summary: Under severe data limits, additional parameters or repeated training can worsen held-out language-model performance during pretraining or fine-tuning.

examples.headline: With 100 million tokens, one-epoch models above 2 billion parameters underperform 200 million–1 billion-parameter models.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Data allocation can have an intermediate optimum
related_findings.summary: Generalization or convergence can be best with an intermediate amount of data assigned to a stage, or an intermediate dataset size. The result depends on the task and whether training time is counted in parameter updates or full passes through the data (epochs).

examples.headline: Chest-X-ray active-learning error falls then rises as the first-stage budget share grows, under reported settings.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generative objectives can introduce capacity peaks
related_findings.summary: Supervised objectives or pseudo-supervised objectives (using generated training targets) can introduce peaks in generative models’ performance curves as capacity increases. Objective weights and optimization methods affect the pattern.

examples.headline: Objectives using generated targets produce double descent, including in a nonlinear Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty.

reading_list.why: Compares network width, training duration and sample size, including cases where optimal early stopping prevents added samples from worsening results.
Introduces the general double-descent picture through shallow networks, random Fourier features and forests.
Independently tests width-wise double descent; plotting error against norms (vector lengths) depends on parameter ranges and how capacity is measured.

known_gaps.summary: The main gaps concern unresolved disagreements, unmeasured thresholds for fitting training data exactly, untested mechanisms involving complexity and regularization, and uncertainty about evidence reliability or whether replications are independent.
items: Some apparent disagreements still need comparisons under matched conditions. The disagreement about noiseless logistic classification remains unresolved.

In the pretraining comparison of models with 1.4 billion parameters, results changed direction in ways that depended on the training setup, but no peak was established near an exact fit to the training data. What this implies for the proposed explanation based on regularization, which limits overfitting, remains open.
Some engineering and diffusion-distillation studies report decreasing error without locating the interpolation threshold. These trends do not establish behavior near interpolation.
A theoretical ceiling alone does not show whether actual test error peaks or where a peak lies relative to an exact fit to the training data.

Effective data rank summarizes how many directions contribute substantially to variation in the data. Thresholds based on it have not established a single measure of model complexity that predicts where error peaks.
Some conclusions still depend on disputed source statements or incomplete readings. Their evidential support needs verification.
Some studies listed as separate publications may describe the same work. The extent of independent replication remains uncertain.
